core.title: Wire new behavior through its real owner (no false GREEN)
core.given: a governed ATDD task where the acceptance for newly implemented behavior passes
core.when: the production-reachability (dead-code) check reports a finding on the newly implemented behavior
core.then: Wire the new behavior through its real production owner before you treat it as complete.
avoid: Manufacturing an import edge to fake reachability.
core.why: A production-reachability check can expose a false GREEN: a unit-level acceptance can pass against code that no production entry point can reach.
evidence: The new behavior is reachable from a production entry point through its real owner. No production-reachability finding remains on it, and no artificial import edge was added.
verification: Backed by the stack's production-reachability (dead-code) check, which reports production code that no production entry point can reach. The detector, validator and finding ids of that check are realization details; the core names the check generically.

The check can expose a false GREEN that the passing unit-level acceptance alone does not: a passing acceptance proves the behavior exists, not that any production entry point reaches the code. The core does not claim reachability is the only sensor with this property; such an exclusivity claim is established only within a realization's own sensor family and stays with the realization.

The check reports reachability only. Whether a finding applies to newly implemented behavior, as opposed to pre-existing code, is llm_judged and gates activation, so the check alone does not fire this obligation on pre-existing dead code.

values: finding applies to newly implemented behavior

fires: A unit-level acceptance passes, but the production-reachability check reports that the newly implemented code is unreachable from any production entry point.
doesNotFire: Reachability findings on pre-existing code that the current behavior did not add. The REFACTOR part of phase discipline handles those.

bunOnly.reason: The stack qualifier names the realization; the core says 'governed ATDD task' and the stack is supplied by the profile/realization, not by the core.

bunOnly.text: coder.bun.dead-code-reachability reports a finding on the newly implemented behavior
bunOnly.reason: Names the finding id of the Bun realization's reachability detector; per the closed vocabulary's notProfileKeys, a rule's finding ids stay with the realization and the core names the check generically.

bunOnly.text: dead-code-reachability is the one sensor that can expose a false GREEN
bunOnly.reason: Two realization-specific elements: the sensor's rule id, and the exclusivity claim ('the one sensor'), which is established only within ATDD-Bun's metrics-detector sensor family. The core keeps the non-exclusive claim (reachability can expose a false GREEN) and asserts no exclusivity across another stack's sensors.

bunOnly.text: The new behavior is reachable from a production root through its real owner. No dead-code-reachability finding remains on it
bunOnly.reason: Names the Bun sensor's finding id and ATDD-Bun's local term 'production root' (rendered 'production entry point' in the core). The no-artificial-import-edge condition in the same sentence is general, not Bun-specific, and stays in the core unchanged.

bunOnly.text: Among the seven refactor sensors, only dead-code-reachability can expose a false GREEN: a unit-level acceptance passing against code that no production root reaches.
bunOnly.reason: 'The seven refactor sensors' is the ATDD-Bun metrics-detector family, and the exclusivity claim ('only') holds only within that family; both the family scope and the sensor's finding id are realization-specific. The core's verification keeps only the non-exclusive claim that the reachability check can expose a false GREEN.
The concrete finding id binds the neutral 'production-reachability finding' concept to the Bun realization's detector; another stack binds it to its own check's finding.

classification.note: Neutralized by dropping only the stack qualifier 'Bun'; the gate itself (acceptance for newly implemented behavior passes) is unchanged.
Core names the check generically as the production-reachability (dead-code) check; the finding id coder.bun.dead-code-reachability is a realization detail kept in bunOnly.
Fully stack-neutral; kept verbatim. The single obligation.

The mechanism (a passing unit-level acceptance does not prove any production entry point reaches the code) is neutral and goes to the core without exclusivity; the sensor id and the 'one sensor' exclusivity claim are scoped to the Bun sensor family and kept in bunOnly.
Kept verbatim: manufacturing an import edge is the cross-stack anti-pattern (module imports exist in most stacks), so it is not Bun-specific and is not broadened to all dependency edges.

Same three evidence conditions (reachable through the real owner from a production entry point, no remaining reachability finding, no artificial import edge); only the detector finding id and the local term 'production root' are Bun bindings kept in bunOnly.
The non-exclusive claim (the reachability check can expose a false GREEN) goes to core:verification; the family scope ('seven refactor sensors') and the exclusivity claim ('only') are Bun-only.
Stack-neutral gate (governed work driven by a behavioral acceptance); kept unchanged.
Core fact value names the finding kind; the concrete finding id is the Bun binding, kept in bunOnly.
Stack-neutral gate (finding hits code added for the current behavior); kept unchanged, still llm_judged.
ATDD loop phases (GREEN, REFACTOR, review) are stack-neutral loop vocabulary; values and observability kept.

neutralityNotes: Fully neutralizable; no profile keys were needed. The core's only concrete reference is the stack's reachability check, which it names generically (production-reachability / dead-code), because per the closed vocabulary's notProfileKeys the detector and finding ids of a rule are realization details, not profile data; nothing else in the rule points at paths, suffixes or tools. Renderings fixed per round-2 audit: 'import edge' is kept verbatim in the core (module imports exist across stacks, so it is neither Bun-only nor broadened to all dependency edges, and avoid[0] is no longer classified bunOnly); ATDD-Bun's 'production root' is rendered 'production entry point'; the sensor name 'dead-code-reachability' is treated as the stack-neutral dead-code/production-reachability concept, with the concrete rule id kept only in the realization. The exclusivity claim ('the one sensor' / 'only dead-code-reachability') is established only within ATDD-Bun's seven-refactor-sensor family, so it is kept only in bunOnly (for why and verifier_detail[0]) while core:why and core:verification state the non-exclusive claim that the reachability check can expose a false GREEN. ATDD loop terms (RED/GREEN/REFACTOR, review) and 'governed ATDD task' are treated as stack-neutral loop vocabulary. Instantiating the core with the Bun bindings recorded in bunOnly reproduces bun.json exactly: same gates, same fires/doesNotFire scope, same obligation and anti-pattern, no exception dropped and none added.
